title: Graph BFS: shortest hops
summary: Fewest edges from start to every reachable node. Mark a node when you enqueue it, not when you dequeue it; distances[node] + 1 carries the level, so no per-level loop is needed. O(V + E).
code: # FIFO order reaches nodes in order of distance.
triggers: fewest steps, hops or moves when every edge costs the same
spread outward level by level from one or many sources
prompts: A subway map lists which stations connect directly. Report the fewest rides from your station to each station you can reach.
In a professional network, list everyone within three introductions of you, with how many introductions each one needs.
invariant: Nodes leave the queue in nondecreasing distance, so the first distance recorded for a node is final.
mantra: Mark when you enqueue, not when you dequeue.
pitfalls: Marking on dequeue lets a node enter the queue many times.
Per-level work needs for _ in range(len(queue)) inside while queue.
Weighted edges need Dijkstra, not BFS.

anchors.name: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
anchors.trick: Level loop: for _ in range(len(queue)) collects one level.

anchors.name: Rotting Oranges
anchors.trick: Multi-source: enqueue every rotten cell first; minutes = levels.

anchors.name: Word Ladder
anchors.trick: Words are nodes, one-letter changes are edges; BFS gives the fewest steps.

mutations.explanation: LIFO order is depth-first: a node reached first along a longer path keeps that longer distance.
